title: 水位与 lmkd 调参：min_free_kbytes、watermark_scale_factor、lmkd 属性与风险
key_conclusions: Watermark and lmkd tuning must be driven by stable lab evidence, not isolated kill logs.
Watermark knobs change reclaim timing and reserve pressure, but they do not identify the leaking or growing memory bucket.
lmkd properties express tradeoffs between stalls and kills; they do not prove root cause.
A tuning change is acceptable only when PSI, vmstat, ZRAM, lmkd, and user experience improve together.
shallow_points: The article does not validate property names and defaults on a specific Android branch.
It does not include measured before/after tuning data from a low-end device.
It does not provide automated rollback tooling.
It does not quantify safe ranges for each RAM class.
discovered_connections: Day 61's lab becomes the acceptance gate for every tuning experiment.
Day 60's trim and compaction checks must run before lmkd thresholds are changed.
Day 59's ZRAM model explains why fewer kills can still increase swap-in stalls.
Day 63 should treat critical process protection as policy evidence, not as a shortcut around pressure reduction.
suggest_future_topics: Day 63 should explain adj design, binding relationships, foreground services, and abuse boundaries for critical process protection.
Day 64 should replay a low-watermark jank case with baseline, one-knob change, rollback, and before/after evidence.
A future appendix should add branch-specific lmkd property defaults and sysctl snapshots.
Day 65 should use the same one-knob discipline before changing kill thresholds for high-priority victims.
knowledge_gaps: Need Android-version-specific validation for lmkd properties and kernel watermark behavior.
Need measured tuning results across 2GB, 3GB, and 4GB devices.
Need automated scripts to snapshot, modify, validate, and rollback sysctl/property changes.
Need examples where tuning decreases kill rate but increases PSI or ZRAM hot swap-in.
